p2_p3_fresh_discovery.the_question: What technical operation must occur when an AI medical-device model changes that existing 2026 PCCP, monitoring, eQMS, validation and regulatory systems cannot perform cheaply?

the_candidate_mechanism.name: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED)
the_candidate_mechanism.formulation: Given a proposed ML model modification, automatically determine the minimum sufficient validation evidence needed to establish that the modification remains within the previously authorized safety/effectiveness envelope, and prove why that evidence is sufficient.

the_4_link_chain.name: Change → Clinical Pathways
the_4_link_chain.description: Map the ML model modification to the affected clinical pathways (which patient journeys, which decision points, which outcomes are touched by this change).
the_4_link_chain.prior_art_coverage: ML change-impact (influence functions, datamodels) maps to training data/subpopulations, NOT to clinical pathways. Clinical pathway modeling exists as a separate field. NO BRIDGE between them.
the_4_link_chain.gap_status: ESSENTIALLY ABSENT — most novel structural contribution

the_4_link_chain.name: Risk-Envelope Propagation
the_4_link_chain.description: Propagate the change through the clinical risk model to determine which risks are affected and how.
the_4_link_chain.prior_art_coverage: ISO 14971 FMEA and assurance-case structures exist, but are manually authored. No auto-propagation from an ML change through a clinical risk model.
the_4_link_chain.gap_status: PARTIAL — risk models exist but not auto-propagated from ML change

the_4_link_chain.name: Minimum Sufficient Evidence Derivation
the_4_link_chain.description: Derive the smallest set of validation tests that proves safety within the affected risk envelope.
the_4_link_chain.prior_art_coverage: BOED, active testing, subset selection, NI testing all exist but optimize for information gain / estimation accuracy, NOT for safety sufficiency within a risk envelope.
the_4_link_chain.gap_status: PARTIAL/FRAGMENTED — each optimizes a different objective; none derive a safety-sufficient minimum set for a modification

the_4_link_chain.name: Sufficiency Proof
the_4_link_chain.description: Prove why the chosen evidence set is sufficient (not just 'we ran some tests') — a formal sufficiency argument.
the_4_link_chain.prior_art_coverage: Assurance cases (GSN) exist but are manually authored. Conformal/PAC guarantees are population-level, not modification-specific. Certified robustness is for input perturbations, not evidence sufficiency.
the_4_link_chain.gap_status: GAP — rarest and most defensible element. No automated, modification-specific, clinical-risk-aware sufficiency proof exists.

the_candidate_mechanism.the_integrated_mechanism: The full chain: change → clinical pathways → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof. No existing 2026 technology performs this chain end-to-end and automatically.

domains_searched: Sequential test reuse in regulatory science
Minimum sufficient evidence in regulatory science (least burdensome)
Model modification validation for medical devices
prior_art_collision_search.verdict: CANDIDATE SURVIVES — full chain not covered by any existing technology
prior_art_collision_search.the_kill_test: Does any existing 2026 technology or research perform the FULL chain automatically (change → clinical pathways → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof)?
prior_art_collision_search.the_answer: NO. The candidate is NOT killed.
what_is_covered: PCCP framework and documentation (FDA guidance, Dec 2024)
Drift detection and performance monitoring (Fiddler, Arize, WhyLabs)
eQMS and design controls (Greenlight Guru, MasterControl)
Regulatory consulting for PCCP authoring (NAMSA, RQM+)
ML change-impact to training data (influence functions, datamodels)
BOED for information gain (not safety sufficiency)
Active testing for performance estimation (not safety proof)
Assurance cases for manual sufficiency arguments (GSN)
what_is_NOT_covered: Automated bridge from ML change to clinical pathways (link 1→2)
Auto-propagation of change through clinical risk model (link 2)
Derivation of safety-sufficient (not info-optimal) minimum evidence set (link 3)
strongest_partial_collision_risks: BOED / active testing (Foster, Ivanova; Kossen, Farquhar) — closest in spirit but optimizes information gain, not safety sufficiency
Conformal risk control (Bates, Angelopoulos) — gives guarantees but population-level, not modification-specific
Assurance case automation (Hawkins, Graydon, Denney) — could partially collide on link 4 if extended to ML + minimum-evidence derivation
prior_art_collision_search.defensible_novel_contribution: The integrated chain + automated sufficiency proof, with the change→clinical-pathway→risk-envelope bridge being the least-contested gap. Link 3 (BOED/active learning) may be used internally as a component, but the objective function (safety sufficiency, not information gain) is the differentiator.

honest_status.overall: STRONG NOVEL HYPOTHESIS — survives prior-art collision, but is NOT yet validated, NOT yet buyer-proven, NOT yet sellable. The collision search is based on training knowledge through early 2025; specific 2025-2026 publications should be verified.

p4_commercial_portfolio.portfolio_generation_rule: Each candidate must immediately have: buyer + pain + existing alternative + missing mechanism + technical effect + economic unit + build-vs-buy + novelty attack + validation route. No candidate enters the active commercial portfolio merely because it sounds valuable.

candidates.name: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED)
candidates.buyer: AI/ML medical-device companies with PCCP obligations (any company modifying models post-market)
candidates.pain: Each model modification requires full re-validation costing $50K-$200K and 4-12 weeks (INDUSTRY ESTIMATE, not FDA-verified). No way to determine if a smaller validation set would suffice.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual risk assessment by regulatory + clinical + ML teams. Full re-validation by default. PCCP authoring consultancies.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Automated derivation of minimum sufficient evidence + sufficiency proof. The 4-link chain (change → clinical pathways → risk envelope → minimum evidence → sufficiency proof).
candidates.technical_effect: Reduces validation cost and time by deriving the MINIMUM sufficient evidence instead of defaulting to full re-validation.
candidates.economic_unit: One model modification validation cycle. Current cost: $50K-$200K (INDUSTRY ESTIMATE). Target: reduce by 50-80% by deriving minimum sufficient subset.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Building internally requires: clinical pathway modeling expertise + risk propagation expertise + BOED/active learning expertise + assurance case automation. 4 rare skill sets. 12-24 months internal build. $500K-$2M+.
candidates.novelty_attack: SURVIVES prior-art collision (P3 above). Full chain not covered by any 2026 technology. Strongest partial collision: BOED/active testing (different objective), assurance case automation (not ML-specific).
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: implement the 4-link chain on 2-3 published model modification datasets. Gate 2: buyer disclosure of actual validation cost. Gate 3: §103 on the integrated chain.

candidates.name: Clinical Pathway Change-Impact Mapper
candidates.buyer: AI/ML medical-device companies + clinical validation teams
candidates.pain: When a model changes, no one knows which clinical pathways are affected. Manual review is incomplete.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual clinical review by medical affairs team.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Automated bridge from ML model change → affected clinical pathways (link 1 of the MSVED chain).
candidates.technical_effect: Maps model behavior delta to clinical decision points and patient journeys.
candidates.economic_unit: One avoided missed-pathway = one avoided post-market safety event ($500K-$50M).
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires clinical ontology + ML change-impact expertise. Niche. 6-12 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: Link 1→2 is the LEAST CONTESTED gap. No prior art bridges ML change to clinical pathways.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: map changes for 2-3 published model modifications with known clinical impacts.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — component of MSVED (CC-01), can be standalone

candidates.name: Safety-Sufficient Subset Selector (vs BOED)
candidates.buyer: ML validation teams at medical-device companies
candidates.pain: BOED/active testing optimizes for information gain, not safety. No tool selects the minimum validation set that proves SAFETY.
candidates.existing_alternative: BOED (Foster, Ivanova), active testing (Kossen), core-set selection. All optimize wrong objective.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Subset selection with safety-sufficiency objective (not information gain). Link 3 of MSVED.
candidates.technical_effect: Selects minimum test set where passing = safety proven within risk envelope.
candidates.economic_unit: Reduction in validation testing cost per modification (subset vs full test suite).
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires formal safety specification + subset optimization. 6-9 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: MUST differentiate from BOED/active testing. Objective function is the differentiator (safety sufficiency vs information gain). Partial collision risk — must be carefully §103'd.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: compare safety-sufficient subset vs BOED-optimal subset on same dataset. Must prove they are DIFFERENT and safety-sufficient is BETTER for regulatory purpose.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — component of MSVED (CC-01), highest collision risk

candidates.name: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator
candidates.buyer: Regulatory affairs teams at AI-device companies
candidates.pain: FDA asks 'why is this evidence sufficient?' and the answer is a manual narrative. No formal proof.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual assurance cases (GSN). Authored by safety engineers. Not ML-specific. Not tied to minimum-evidence derivation.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Automated, modification-specific, clinical-risk-aware sufficiency proof. Link 4 of MSVED.
candidates.technical_effect: Generates a formal sufficiency argument (GSN-like) that is machine-checkable and tied to the derived minimum evidence set.
candidates.economic_unit: One avoided FDA deficiency letter asking 'why is this sufficient?' = $250K-$1M (FDA cost data VERIFIED for 510(k); PMA higher).
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires formal methods + assurance case expertise + ML validation expertise. Very rare. 9-18 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: Link 4 is the RAREST and MOST DEFENSIBLE element. Assurance case automation exists but not for ML modifications + not tied to minimum-evidence derivation. Must verify Hawkins/Graydon/Denney work hasn't extended here.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: generate sufficiency proof for 2-3 model modifications. Have regulatory expert assess if proof would satisfy FDA.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — component of MSVED (CC-01), most defensible

candidates.name: PCCP Modification Bound-Checker
candidates.pain: No way to formally verify that a proposed modification is within the PCCP's agreed scope. Manual review risks out-of-scope changes triggering new submissions.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual review by regulatory team against PCCP document.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Formal verification that a proposed modification is within PCCP boundaries (noted as Gap 3 in earlier analysis).
candidates.technical_effect: Formal specification of PCCP boundaries + automated verification of proposed changes against those boundaries.
candidates.economic_unit: One avoided unnecessary new submission = $200K-$5M (VERIFIED FDA cost range).
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires formal specification expertise + PCCP regulatory expertise. 4-6 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: NOT covered by existing PCCP tools (they help AUTHOR the PCCP, not VERIFY modifications against it). Must verify no formal methods work has addressed this.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: formalize 2-3 PCCP boundaries and verify modifications against them.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — adjacent to MSVED, can be standalone

candidates.name: Subgroup Regression Detector for Modifications
candidates.buyer: ML fairness/regulatory teams at medical-device companies
candidates.pain: A model modification can improve overall performance but WORSEN performance on a subgroup. Current tools detect bias at one point in time, not REGRESSION across modifications.
candidates.existing_alternative: Bias testing tools (AIF360, Fairlearn) — test bias once, not paired across modifications.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Paired subgroup analysis with statistical power calculation across model versions.
candidates.technical_effect: Detects subgroup regression: did the new version perform worse on any subgroup than the old version?
candidates.economic_unit: One avoided subgroup harm event = $500K-$50M (recall + liability).
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires biostatistics + subgroup analysis expertise. 3-6 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: Bias testing tools exist but do NOT do paired regression across modifications. Must verify no 2025-2026 work has added this.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: apply to 2-3 published model modifications with known subgroup impacts.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — component of MSVED, can be standalone

candidates.name: Evidence Chain-of-Custody for FDA Inspection
candidates.buyer: QA/regulatory teams preparing for FDA inspection
candidates.pain: FDA inspection requires tracing every modification → validation → decision → deployment. Current practice: manual documentation in eQMS. No tamper-evident chain.
candidates.existing_alternative: eQMS document management (Greenlight Guru, MasterControl). Manual chain-of-custody.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Tamper-evident, hash-committed chain-of-custody linking model artifact → validation data → statistical result → decision → deployment record.
candidates.technical_effect: Produces an FDA-inspection-ready audit trail that is cryptographically verifiable.
candidates.economic_unit: One avoided FDA 483 observation / warning letter = $500K-$50M (recall + remediation).
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires hash-commitment expertise + QMS integration. 4-6 months build. Buildable but annoying.
candidates.novelty_attack: eQMS tools do document management but not tamper-evident ML evidence chains. Blockchain-adjacent but for ML evidence, not financial. Must verify no eQMS vendor has added this.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: build chain for 2-3 modification cycles. Have QA expert assess inspection-readiness.

candidates.name: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine for Model Modifications
candidates.pain: PCCP requires demonstrating each modification is non-inferior to prior version. No automated tool produces FDA-grade NI statistics with pre-registered margins.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual biostatistics analysis. Generic NI testing (ICH E9) but not packaged for ML model modifications.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins, proper multiple-testing correction, FDA-grade reporting.
candidates.technical_effect: Produces FDA-submission-grade NI statistics for each model modification.
candidates.economic_unit: One avoided statistical deficiency in submission = $250K-$1M.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires biostatistics + ML expertise. 3-6 months build. Modest build cost.
candidates.novelty_attack: NI testing is standard (ICH E9). The AUTOMATION + ML-specific packaging is the novelty. Must verify no commercial tool has automated this for ML.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: apply to 2-3 model modifications with known NI outcomes.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — component of MSVED, moderate collision risk

candidates.name: Clinical Risk Model Propagator
candidates.buyer: Clinical affairs + ML teams at medical-device companies
candidates.pain: When a model changes, the clinical risk model (ISO 14971 FMEA) must be updated manually. No automatic propagation.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual FMEA update by clinical affairs team.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Auto-propagation of ML model change through the clinical risk model. Link 2 of MSVED.
candidates.technical_effect: Updates the risk model automatically based on the model behavior delta.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires clinical risk modeling + ML expertise. 6-9 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: ISO 14971 FMEA is standard but manual. Auto-propagation from ML change is novel. Must verify no risk management software has added ML propagation.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: propagate 2-3 model changes through a published clinical risk model.

candidates.name: Modification Impact Assessor for PCCP
candidates.buyer: Regulatory teams writing PCCP impact assessments
candidates.pain: PCCP requires an impact assessment for each modification type. Current practice: manual narrative. No quantitative impact prediction.
candidates.existing_alternative: Manual impact assessment by regulatory + clinical teams.
candidates.missing_mechanism: Quantitative prediction of modification impact on safety/effectiveness, derived from the model change.
candidates.technical_effect: Produces a quantitative impact assessment that feeds into the PCCP documentation.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Requires ML + regulatory expertise. 4-6 months build.
candidates.novelty_attack: Impact assessment is required by PCCP guidance but no tool automates it quantitatively. Must verify no PCCP tool has added quantitative impact prediction.
candidates.validation_route: Gate 1: predict impact for 2-3 modifications with known outcomes.
candidates.portfolio_status: ACTIVE — component of MSVED, PCCP-specific framing
